plan: In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors. This is because you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid, and you pay that second-highest bid, not your own bid—so there's no incentive to shade your bid up or down. With a private value of $9, I will bid exactly $9 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction, where bidding one's true value is the dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies. Since I don't win-or-lose based on my own bid amount directly but rather pay the second-highest bid if I win, bidding exactly my value ensures I never overpay (I only win when profitable) and never miss profitable wins. Therefore, I will bid my true value of $9.

This is a second-price sealed-bid auction (highest bidder wins, pays second-highest bid). In such auctions, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what others do, since you only pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid. Overbidding risks paying more than the item is worth; underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities. With no prior round history to adjust for, I'll bid exactly my value of $34.
